label: alternative
why_suggested: This was the best-scoring option that uses different main crops from the recommended plan in at least two of the three years, so you have a real alternative.
It scores 76 out of 100. Its strongest points are pest and disease break (100) and heat and frost resilience (100).
Its weakest point is estimated revenue (51).

evidence.fact: water fit 82; soil health 71; heat and frost resilience 100; estimated revenue 51; animal feed value 56; pest and disease break 100
A crop is growing in about 7 of 12 months in a typical year.
Roots reach about 90 cm on average.
Based on 10 years of monthly weather (synthetic demonstration data).
The thirstiest year needs about 186 mm of irrigation on top of rain; your yearly water budget is 300 mm.
Replaying 10 past years, the typical score is 77 and the lowest is 73 (year 2022).

benefits: Includes legumes (Faba bean). Legumes host bacteria that fix nitrogen from the air, which can reduce the nitrogen the next crop needs.
Cover crops (Oat (cover crop)) keep the soil covered and roots alive between main crops, which helps protect against erosion and adds plant residue.
Every year of this plan fits within your yearly water budget.
Consecutive crops come from different plant families, which helps break pest and disease cycles.
data_gaps: Weather and soil data are synthetic
Income compares estimated revenue per hectare, not profit. Production costs are not included.
Each crop uses one average water coefficient instead of stage-by-stage values.
Sowing windows, yields and prices are typical values, not your local calendar or market.
Soil values come from a regional dataset, not from samples of your own field.
Scores are modeled estimates, not certified results.
risks_needing_local_review: Needs irrigation: Potato (irrigated). Check that you can reliably get the water.
Water stress appears in 5 crop-months across the three years.
Check varieties, fertilizer and pest advice with your local agricultural advisor before changing your rotation.

reasons: Weather and soil data are synthetic

disclaimer: This tool supports farmer judgment and does not replace local expertise.
